p.src: Now Song Jiang, having parted from Liu Tang, walked leisurely back to his lodgings through the moonlit streets. As chance would have it, he met Madam Yan, who hurried up and called, “Secretary, I have sent for you time and again, but such an important gentleman is hard indeed to see! Even if that wretched girl of mine spoke out of turn and offended you, Secretary, please show some regard for this old woman. I shall discipline her and make her apologize to you. By good fortune I have met you tonight, Secretary, so come home with me.” Song Jiang said, “I am overwhelmed with county-office business today and cannot get away. I shall come another day.” Madam Yan said, “That will never do. My daughter is at home waiting especially for you. Just go and pay her a brief visit. How can you be so heartless!” Song Jiang said, “I truly am rather busy. I promise I shall come tomorrow.” Madam Yan said, “Tonight I insist that you come with me.” She seized Song Jiang by the sleeve and protested, “Who has been turning you against us? My daughter and I depend upon you for our livelihood through the rest of our days. Pay no heed to the idle gossip and slander of outsiders; judge the matter for yourself. If my daughter has done anything wrong, lay all the blame on me. Please, Secretary, just come with me this once.” Song Jiang said, “Stop pestering me. I cannot leave my duties unattended here.” Madam Yan said, “Even if you delay some official business, surely the magistrate will not punish you for it. If we miss this chance, another may be hard to find. You simply must come home with me; once we arrive, I have something to tell you.” Song Jiang was a man of impatient temper. Unable to endure the old woman’s importunity, he said, “Let go of me. I shall come.” Madam Yan said, “Do not run off, Secretary. An old woman cannot keep up with you.” Song Jiang said, “Must you carry on so!” The two followed close upon each other until they reached her door. Indeed:

p.src: Song Jiang stopped in his tracks. Madam Yan barred his way with an outstretched arm and said, “Now that you have come this far, Secretary, you surely cannot refuse to go inside.” Song Jiang went in and sat on a stool. The old woman was cunning—for as the ancient saying goes, “Who can escape the clutches of an old procuress?” Afraid that Song Jiang might leave, she sat close beside him and called, “Daughter, your beloved Third Brother is here!” Yan Poxi was lying on her bed before a solitary lamp, with nothing to occupy her thoughts, waiting only for Little Zhang the Third to come. She heard her mother call, “Your beloved Third Brother is here!” The woman assumed it was Zhang the Third. She sprang up, hurriedly smoothed her cloudlike coiffure with one hand, and muttered curses: “That doomed wretch! How cruelly he has kept me waiting! I shall begin by slapping his face twice!” She flew downstairs and peered through the lattice. The glazed lamp in the hall shone brightly, revealing Song Jiang. At once she turned around, went back upstairs, and lay down on the bed as before.

p.src: It was a single upper room six rafters wide. In the front half stood a raised platform, a table, and stools; the rear half was furnished as a bedchamber, with a bed carved in floral patterns on three sides set against the inner wall; it had railings on either side, from which hung a canopy of red gauze; to one side stood a clothes rack with a hand towel draped over it; on this side was a washbasin; upon a gilt-lacquered table stood a pewter lampstand; beside it were two low stools; a portrait of a beautiful lady hung on the wall directly ahead; and opposite the bed four folding chairs were arranged in a row.

Madam Yan pulled her daughter up from the bed and said, “The Secretary is here. Daughter, that temper of yours is the trouble. You wound him with your words and anger him so badly that he stops visiting, yet when you have time you brood over him at home. Now that I have brought him here with such difficulty, instead of getting up and saying a conciliatory word, you show your temper again!” Poxi flung her hand away and said to the old woman, “Why are you making such a damned commotion? I have done nothing wrong! He is the one who stopped coming. Why should I apologize to him?”

p.src: Song Jiang heard this but said nothing. The old woman pushed a folding chair close beside Song Jiang, then urged her daughter forward, saying, “Sit with Third Brother for a while. If you will not apologize, so be it, but do not lose your temper. You two have not seen each other for so long; at least exchange one affectionate word.” But the woman refused to come near and instead sat down opposite Song Jiang. Song Jiang lowered his head and said nothing. When the old woman looked at her daughter, she too had turned her face away. Madam Yan said, “Without wine or drink, how can we conduct the ceremony? I have a flask of good wine here. I shall buy some fruit so that you may entertain the Secretary properly. Daughter, sit here and keep the Secretary company. Do not be shy; I shall be back soon.” Song Jiang thought to himself, “This old woman has me pinned down, and I cannot get away. Once she goes downstairs, I shall leave right behind her.” The old woman perceived that Song Jiang meant to leave. After stepping out of the room, she saw the door had a hasp, so she pulled it shut and fastened the hasp. Song Jiang thought privately, “That damned old procuress has outwitted me first.”

p.src: Now Yan Po went downstairs. First she went to the kitchen and lit a lamp. A pot of water for washing feet was already heating on the stove, so she added a little more firewood. Then, taking some small pieces of silver, she went out of the lane and bought fresh seasonal fruit, fresh fish, tender chicken, fat salted fish, and the like. When she returned home, she arranged everything on plates; she poured the wine into a basin, ladled half a measure into a vessel, warmed it in the pot, and poured it into a wine flask. She prepared several dishes, three wine cups, three pairs of chopsticks, and loaded them all onto a tray, which she carried upstairs and set on the landing table. She opened the door, carried everything inside, and set it out on the table. When she looked at Song Jiang, he merely hung his head; when she looked at her daughter, she too was facing away. Yan Po said, “Daughter, get up and offer him a cup of wine.” Poxi said, “Drink it yourselves. I cannot be bothered!” The old woman said, “Daughter, your parents have indulged your temper since childhood, but you cannot behave this way before other people.” Poxi said, “What will happen if I refuse to offer him wine? Surely no flying sword will come and take off my head!” The old woman burst out laughing instead and said, “So it is my fault again. The clerk is a gallant gentleman and will not stoop to quarrel with you. If you will not pour the wine, so be it; at least turn around and drink a cup.” But Poxi still would not turn her head. The old woman then poured wine and urged Song Jiang to drink. Reluctantly, he drank one cup. The old woman smiled and said, “Please do not take offense, Clerk. Let us put all idle talk aside; tomorrow I shall explain everything at leisure. When outsiders see you here, some spiteful good-for-nothings may resent it and spout all manner of foul nonsense. Pay them no heed, Clerk, and just enjoy your wine.” She poured three cups and set them on the table, saying, “Daughter, do not act like a child. Just drink a cup, never mind how.” Poxi said, “Stop pestering me! I am full and cannot drink.” Yan Po said, “Daughter, surely you can keep your Third Brother company and drink one cup with him.”

p.src: As Poxi listened, she thought to herself, “My heart belongs wholly to Zhang San. Who has the patience to keep this brute company? If I do not get him drunk, he is certain to pester me.” Poxi had no choice but to pick up her wine reluctantly and drink half a cup. The old woman smiled and said, “Daughter, you are merely out of sorts. Open your heart, drink another cup or two, and then sleep. You too, Clerk, drain a few full cups.” Unable to withstand her urging, Song Jiang drank three or five cups in succession. The old woman also drank several cups one after another, then went downstairs again to warm more wine.

p.src: The old woman had been displeased to see her daughter refusing to drink, but when she finally saw her relent and take some wine, she rejoiced, thinking, “If she can only keep him here tonight, he will forget all his anger and resentment. Let her keep him entangled a while longer, and afterward we can consider what to do.” Thinking thus, the old woman drank three great goblets of wine by the stove. Feeling a pleasant tingling come over her, she poured herself another bowl and drank it. Then she ladled out more than half a measure, poured it into the wine pot, and clambered upstairs. There she found Song Jiang sitting silent with his head bowed, while her daughter had turned her face aside and was fiddling with her skirt. The old woman laughed loudly and said, “Neither of you is made of clay, so why are you both sitting there without a word? Clerk, you are a man, after all. You ought to show some tenderness and amuse her with a few words of love.” Song Jiang could think of no way out. He said nothing, but inwardly felt trapped, unable either to advance or retreat. Yan Poxi thought to herself, “You ignore me and expect me, as on ordinary days, to come talk with you and keep you company with jokes and laughter. Well, today I will not oblige you.” Having drunk so much, the old woman kept babbling incoherently, gossiping about the Zhang family and the Li family and prattling about anything and everything. p.src: Now in Yuncheng County there was a seller of fermented pickles named Second Brother Tang, also called Tang Niu'er. He was usually to be found idling about the streets as a hanger-on, and Song Jiang often gave him money to help him along. Whenever he brought Song Jiang word of some official business, he would also come away with a few strings of cash to spend. Whenever Song Jiang needed him, he would risk his life and press forward. Late that evening, after losing at gambling and finding himself at his wits' end, he went to the county offices in search of Song Jiang, then hurried to his lodgings but could not find him there. The neighbors all asked, “Second Brother Tang, whom are you looking for? Why are you in such a hurry?” Tang Niu'er said, “My need is urgent. I am looking for my patron, but I cannot find him anywhere.” They asked, “Who is this patron of yours?” Tang Niu'er said, “Clerk Song at the county offices.” They said, “I just saw him walking past with Yan Po.” Tang Niu'er said, “That explains it. That vile slut Yan Poxi and Zhang San are as hot for each other as two lumps of fire, and the only person they keep in the dark is Clerk Song. He must have heard some rumor of it, for he has not visited her in a good while. Tonight that old hag must have pretended some excuse and pestered him into going with her. I have no money to spend and am desperate. I will go there and somehow get a few strings of cash from him, and cadge a couple of bowls of wine besides.” He went straight to Yan Po's door. A lamp shone inside, and the door had been left open. When he reached the foot of the narrow stairs, he heard Yan Po laughing heartily upstairs. Tang Niu'er crept silently upstairs and peered through a crack in the board wall. He saw Song Jiang and Poxi both sitting with their heads bowed; the old woman sat at the head of the table, babbling endlessly about seventy-three things and eighty-four more.

p.src: Tang Niu'er slipped into the room, bowed three times to Yan Po, Song Jiang, and Poxi, and stood to one side. Song Jiang thought, “This fellow could not have come at a better time.” He jerked his lips toward the stairs. Tang Niu'er was quick-witted and understood the signal at once. Looking at Song Jiang, he said, “There is nowhere your humble servant has not searched for you, yet here you are drinking and amusing yourself, comfortably taking your ease!” Song Jiang said, “Can there be some urgent matter at the county offices?” Tang Niu'er said, “Clerk, how could you have forgotten? It is that case from this morning. His Honor the magistrate is raging in the hall and has sent four or five relays of constables to your lodgings to find you. They have searched everywhere without success, and His Honor is beside himself with impatience. You must set out at once.” Song Jiang said, “If it is that urgent, I have no choice but to go.” He rose to go downstairs, but the old woman barred his way, saying, “Clerk, do not try that trick. Tang Niu'er has come to spin you a tale, but even you crafty rogues cannot fool this old lady! This is truly ‘brandishing a great axe in Master Lu Ban's own hands!’ At this hour the magistrate will already have returned to his private quarters to drink and make merry with his wife. What official business could possibly send him into a rage? Such a story might deceive a goblin, but it will not pass muster with this old lady.”

p.src: Granny Yan said, “What filthy nonsense! These eyes of mine are as clear as glass gourds. Just now I saw the clerk purse his lips at you, telling you to make a scene; yet instead of urging him into my daughter’s room, you tried to drive him away. As the saying goes, ‘Murder may be pardoned, but an outrage against all reason cannot be endured.’” The old woman sprang up, thrust one hand against Tang Niu’er’s neck, and sent him staggering straight out of the room and down the stairs. Tang Niu’er said, “Why are you shoving me?” The old woman shouted, “Don’t you know that ruining a person’s trade and livelihood is like killing their parents, wife, and children? Raise your voice again and I’ll beat you, you thieving beggar!” Tang Niu’er pushed his way back and said, “Go on, hit me!” Emboldened by drink, the old woman spread her five fingers and slapped Tang Niu’er twice across the face, knocking him clean beyond the curtain. She pulled aside the curtain and tossed it behind the door, shut both door leaves, fastened the bar, and went on cursing.

p.src: Now, dear reader, you should know that nothing is more fearsome than carnal desire. p.src: Half a watch later, he heard Poxi give a cold laugh from the other end of the bed. Song Jiang was angry and stifled at heart; how could he possibly fall asleep? As the old saying goes, “In pleasure we resent the night’s brevity; in loneliness we hate the watches’ length.” By the time the third watch approached midnight, the wine had worn off. He endured until the fifth watch, then rose, washed his face with cold water from the basin, put on his outer clothes and headcloth, and cursed aloud, “You shameless wretch, how utterly rude you are!” Poxi had not slept either. Hearing Song Jiang curse her, she turned around and retorted, “Have you no shame, showing that face of yours?” Song Jiang suppressed his anger and went downstairs. Granny Yan heard his footsteps and called from her bed, “Clerk, sleep a little longer and wait until daylight before you go. Why get up at the fifth watch for no reason?” Song Jiang did not answer and merely went on opening the door. The old woman said again, “Clerk, when you go out, pull the door shut for me.” Song Jiang went out and pulled it shut behind him. With no place to vent the anger he had swallowed, he headed straight back toward his lodgings. But as he passed before the county offices, he saw a lamp burning. Looking closer, he found it was Old Wang, the seller of medicinal broth, who had come before the yamen to catch the early market.

p.src: When the old man saw Song Jiang coming, he hurriedly asked, “How is it that you are out so early today, Constable?” Song Jiang said, “I was drunk last night and misheard the watch drum.” Old Wang said, “You must be suffering from the wine. Please have a bowl of two-cured-herb soup to sober you.” Song Jiang said, “That would be excellent.” He sat down on a stool. The old man served him a strong bowl of two-cured-herb soup and handed it to Song Jiang to drink. After drinking it, Song Jiang suddenly thought, “I often take his medicinal soups, yet he has never asked me to pay. I once promised him a coffin, but I have never given him one. Yesterday Chao Gai sent me gold, and I accepted one bar, which is in my document pouch. Why not give it to the old man for his coffin and make him happy?” Song Jiang then said, “Old Wang, some time ago I promised you the price of a coffin, but all this while I have failed to give it to you. Today I have some gold here. Take it to Chen Sanlang’s house, buy a coffin, and keep it at home. When you reach the end of your allotted years, I shall give you something more for your funeral expenses.” Old Wang said, “Benefactor, you have always looked after this old fellow, and now you even bestow upon me the coffin for my final rest. I cannot repay you in this life; in the next I shall become your donkey or horse and repay you, Constable.” Song Jiang said, “Do not speak so.” But when he lifted the front of his outer robe to take out the document pouch, he started in alarm and cried, “Disaster! Last night I left it on the bedstead rail in that wretch’s room. I stormed out in anger and never fastened it back around my waist. These few ounces of gold are nothing, but the letter Chao Gai sent was wrapped around it. I had meant to burn it before Liu Tang at the tavern, but if he returned and reported that, they would only think I cared nothing for Chao Gai. p.src: Now Yan Poxi, hearing that Song Jiang had gone out, scrambled up and muttered to herself, “That scoundrel kept me awake all night with his disturbance. That shameless wretch expected me to humor him and humble myself. Not likely! I am happy enough with Zhang San; who can be bothered to pay attention to you? It would be better if you never came here at all!” Still talking, she spread the bedding, removed her upper jacket, loosened her skirt below, bared her breast, and took off her undergarment. The lamp before the bed was burning brightly, and its light revealed a purple gauze phoenix sash hanging from the bedstead rail. Seeing it, Poxi laughed. “That Black San is endlessly good for a laugh. He has forgotten his phoenix sash here. I shall keep it and give it to Zhang San to wear.” She reached out and lifted it, bringing up the document pouch and a knife as well, and felt that the pouch was rather heavy. She pulled her hand free and gave the pouch a single shake over the table, spilling out the packet of gold and the letter. The woman picked it up and, by the lamplight, saw a gleaming yellow bar of gold. Poxi laughed. “Heaven has sent this so Zhang San and I can buy ourselves something good to eat. I have noticed Zhang San growing thin these past few days, and I was just thinking of buying him something nourishing.” She set down the gold, unfolded the letter, and read it by the lamp. It mentioned Chao Gai and recorded many affairs. Poxi said, “Well, well! I had thought it was always the bucket that fell into the well, but it seems the well may fall into the bucket too. I want Zhang San and me to become man and wife, and you alone stand in our way. Today you have fallen into my hands! So you have been secretly dealing with the bandits of Liangshan Marsh, and they sent you a hundred taels of gold. There is no need to hurry. I shall take my time amusing myself with you.” She wrapped the gold in the letter as before and tucked it back into the document pouch. “Not even the Five Sages could spirit it away from me now.” As she was talking to herself upstairs, she suddenly heard the door below creak open. The old woman called, “Who is it?” Song Jiang answered, “It is I.” The old woman said, “I told you it was early, but you would not believe me and insisted on leaving. So now you have come back because it was too early after all. Go and sleep a while longer with my daughter, and leave at daybreak.” Song Jiang made no reply and rushed straight upstairs.

Why should I not agree to this one?” Poxi said, “Take the hundred taels of gold that Chao Gai of Liangshan Marsh gave you and hand it over at once. Then I shall spare you this matchless capital lawsuit and return the written confession in your document pouch.” Song Jiang said, “I can indeed agree to the other two demands. As for that hundred taels of gold, it was indeed offered to me, but I refused it and had him take it back just as it was. If I truly had it, I would present it to you with both hands.” Poxi said, “Of course you would say that! As the saying goes, ‘An officer seeing money is like a fly seeing blood.’ He sent someone to bring you gold—how could you possibly have turned it away? That claim of yours is nothing but a fart! Of those who serve as officers, ‘what cat does not eat fish?’ ‘Before King Yama, no ghost is ever sent back!’ Whom are you trying to deceive? p.src: In a sudden fit of anger, Song Jiang had killed Yan Poxi. He took the document pouch, drew out the letter, and burned it over the dying lamp. He fastened the phoenix sash around himself and went downstairs. The old woman had been sleeping below. Though she heard the couple quarrelling, she paid it no particular heed. Then she heard her daughter cry once, “Black Third Gentleman is murdering me!” Not knowing what had happened, she sprang up in alarm, put on her clothes, and rushed upstairs, where she collided head-on with Song Jiang. Mother Yan asked, “What are you two making such a commotion about?” Song Jiang said, “Your daughter was far too insolent, so I killed her!” The old woman laughed and said, “What manner of talk is that? Even if your eyes are fierce and you are ill-tempered in drink and forever wanting to kill someone, Clerk, you must not make sport of this old woman.” Song Jiang said, “If you do not believe me, go look in the room. I truly killed her.” The old woman said, “I do not believe you.” But when she pushed open the door and looked inside, she saw the corpse lying stiff in a pool of blood. The old woman cried, “What misery! What am I to do now?” Song Jiang said, “I am a man of mettle! I will not flee, not even if it costs me my life. Do with me as you please.” The old woman said, “That wretch truly was no good, and you were not wrong to kill her, Clerk. It is only that this old woman now has no one to support her.” Song Jiang said, “That is no difficulty. Since you put it so, you need not worry. I possess considerable means and shall see that you have ample food and clothing and live out the rest of your life in comfort.” Mother Yan said, “If so, that is well indeed. I thank you deeply, Clerk. But my daughter lies dead on the bed. How are we to dispose of her remains?” Song Jiang said, “That is easily managed. I shall go to Chen Sanlang’s house and buy you a coffin. When the coroner and undertakers come to place her in it, I shall personally instruct them. I shall also give you ten taels of silver to settle the funeral expenses.” The old woman thanked him, saying, “Clerk, you had best obtain a coffin before daybreak and place her in it, without letting any of the neighbors catch sight of what has happened.” Song Jiang said, “Very well. Bring me paper and brush. I shall write you an order with which to collect it.” Mother Yan said, “A written order will be of no use. You must go and collect it in person, Clerk; only then will they be willing to send it promptly.” Song Jiang said, “What you say is true.”

p.src: The two of them came downstairs. The old woman went into the room for the lock and key, came out to the front door, locked it, and took the key with her. Song Jiang and Old Woman Yan then made their way toward the county offices. It was still early and not yet light, though the county gate had just opened. When the old woman had nearly reached the left side of the county offices, she suddenly seized Song Jiang and shouted, “There is a murderer here!” Song Jiang was thrown into a panic and hurriedly covered her mouth, saying, “Do not shout.” But there was no silencing her. Several constables outside the county offices came running over. When they saw that it was Song Jiang, they tried to persuade her: “Old woman, hold your tongue! Clerk Song is not that sort of man. p.src: Just when there seemed no way out of the predicament, Tang Niu’er happened to come to the county offices with a tray of freshly washed pickled ginger to hawk. There he saw the old woman grappling with Song Jiang and crying out that she had been wronged. When Tang Niu’er saw that it was Old Woman Yan who had seized Song Jiang, he remembered all the foul anger he had swallowed the night before. He set his tray on the bench belonging to Old Wang, the medicine seller, squeezed through the crowd, and shouted, “You old pest, what are you doing, grappling with the clerk?” The old woman said, “Tang the Second, do not come and beat me so he can escape. I will make you answer with your life too!” Tang Niu’er flew into a rage and would not listen to her. He wrenched her hand away and broke her grip; then, without asking what had happened, he spread his five fingers and struck Old Woman Yan full across the face, making her see stars. Dazed by the blow, the old woman had no choice but to let go. Once free, Song Jiang went straight off into the crowd.

p.src: The old woman at once seized Tang Niu’er and cried, “Clerk Song murdered my daughter, and you beat me so he could get away!” Tang Niu’er said in alarm, “How was I to know that?” Old Woman Yan cried, “Gentlemen, please help me catch that murderer! If you do not do so at once, you will surely be implicated too.” The constables, out of regard for Song Jiang, had been unwilling to act against him; but there was no reason for them to delay in arresting Tang Niu’er. They all stepped forward: one held the old woman while three or four seized Tang Niu’er, dragging and hauling him all the way into the Yuncheng county offices. Truly, fortune and calamity have no gate; we summon them ourselves; to fight a fire clad in hemp is to draw the flames upon oneself.
